podcast.body: Released in 1999, this album attempted to prolong the Britpop era at a time when the genre was considered "dead," as the music world had moved on. Despite being a "very good album," its late release meant it struggled to find its place; it would have been a "great album in 1997, not in 1999." The band found itself "stuck" in the Britpop legacy. During this period, Brett Anderson faced severe heroin addiction, which complicated work and tours, alongside ongoing lineup changes and internal discord, with Anderson having a reputation as a "despot" within the band. "intentaba alargar un poco la estela de Britpop cuando ya el Britpop estaba muerto."

Released in 1999, this album still bore the characteristics of a Britpop record. However, it came out in a market where Britpop had been entirely abandoned, marking the beginning of a crisis for the band that would endure for the remainder of their career. "Su idioma en el 99 es que acaba el hip music que seguía haciendo caso en disco de ripop pero ya en un mercado que el ripop estaba totalmente abandonado y aparte tendría una crisis que le duraría el resto de su carrera."
